idea: Train a domain classifier and keep only target-like documents, deduplicated. Steps: (1) Fit TfidfVectorizer(analyzer='char_wb', ngram_range=(1,4), max_features=200k, sublinear_tf=True) on the first 2000 chars of each doc; positives = the 200 target_sample docs, negatives = a seeded random sample of 2000 pool docs (PU-learning style); fit LogisticRegression(class_weight='balanced', C=1). Score all pool docs. (2) Do a second round: retrain with positives = target_sample + top 1500 scored pool docs, negatives = bottom 3000 scored pool docs, rescore. (3) Add cheap WikiText-format features as a boost/override: doc starts with '= ' title line, and contains tokens like ' @-@ ', ' , ', ' . ' (spaced punctuation); also hard-drop junk: docs with <200 chars, spam patterns ('Click here to order', 'best price guaranteed', 'coupon'), low alphabetic ratio (<0.6), or very low unique-word ratio. (4) Remove exact and near duplicates: normalise (lowercase, collapse whitespace) and hash the first 500 chars and the full text; keep one copy per hash. (5) Keep docs with probability > 0.5 (if the threshold yields fewer than ~0.3T tokens, lower it to take the top-scoring docs up to at least 0.5T tokens; measure tokens with tiktoken gpt2). (6) Return the kept indices in a seeded shuffled order; if the kept set is under T tokens, append further independently seeded reshuffles of the same kept set until the list covers T tokens, so training cycles only over clean in-domain text rather than falling back to off-domain docs.
why: The pool is about half spam, code, forum text and other off-domain material while the target is WikiText-style articles with a very distinctive format, so spending all 9.8M training tokens on deduplicated in-domain documents should lower held-out bpb far more than random sampling of the noisy pool.

Apply this drop only to docs that look WikiText-formatted (contain ' , ' and ' . ' spaced punctuation, or start with '= '). For non-WikiText docs use a format-independent check instead: drop if the rate of common function-word bigrams ('of the', 'in the', 'to the', 'on the', 'and the', 'to be', 'it is', 'at the') per 1000 words is below 3. (4) Split survivors into A = WikiText-formatted (spaced punctuation ' , ' and ' . ' at least 5 times per 1000 chars, or ' @-@ ' present, or first line matches '^= .+ =$') and B = other clean English prose. (5) Count tokens with tiktoken gpt2. Selected set = all of A; if A is under T tokens, add B docs in descending order of similarity to the target (cosine between the doc's word-level TF-IDF vector and the centroid of target_sample) until the total reaches 1.05T; do not cycle or repeat anything unless A+B is still under T, in which case append a seeded reshuffle of A. (6) Return the selected set in one seeded random shuffle (A and B mixed).
